'Cars hit by accident' fits the trauma and aligns with the active Memory → Triggers formulation, but 'Sexual situations or intimacy' and 'Arab villages' imply very different trauma contexts (e.g., sexual trauma or combat/terrorism-related threat) that are not represented anywhere else in Memory, Threat, Appraisals, or Strategies. For a 51-year-old male welder whose index trauma is a life-threatening motor vehicle collision, the trigger 'Arab villages' is hard to reconcile clinically with the stated trauma type and the rest of the profile. The memory items all concern vivid sensory/bodily reliving of a crash, which coheres with MVC trauma and the active Memory → Triggers edge, but 'Arab villages' implies a war-zone or ethnopolitical context that is not represented anywhere else in the self-report or formulation. This is a clearly implausible trigger for this trauma profile, unlike the crash imagery and alcohol smell triggers, which could plausibly cue MVC memories.

vignette: Kai had always loved driving on the open road, feeling the freedom that came with cruising down the highway in his trusty ute. But all of that changed one fateful night two years ago when a drunk driver ran a red light and slammed into Kai's vehicle, sending it careening into a nearby pole. The impact was immense, and Kai remembers feeling like he was trapped in a twisted metal coffin, unable to move or escape. As he lay there, dazed and disoriented, the smell of alcohol wafted through the air, mingling with the acrid scent of burning rubber and oil. It's a smell that still haunts him to this day, transporting him back to that moment in time when his life was forever altered. Whenever Kai catches a whiff of booze, he's hit with a wave of anxiety, his heart racing as if he's reliving the crash all over again. The sound of screeching tires and crunching metal is another trigger that sends Kai spiraling back into the past. He'll be working in the yard or driving to work when suddenly the unmistakable sounds of a car accident will pierce the air, making his skin crawl. It's as if his brain is hardwired to respond to these stimuli, instantly conjuring up images of twisted wreckage and shattered glass. Kai tries to avoid certain roads and intersections where accidents are more likely to happen, but it's not always possible. And when he does find himself in situations that trigger memories of the crash, his body seems to take over, reenacting the physical sensations he experienced during the accident. He'll feel a searing pain in his chest, just as he did when the airbag deployed, or his legs will go weak, recalling the feeling of being trapped and helpless. These flashbacks are intense and all-consuming, flooding Kai's senses with sights, sounds, and smells that make it hard for him to distinguish past from present. He'll be standing in the shower, and suddenly he's back in the wreckage, feeling the same rush of adrenaline and terror that coursed through his veins as he struggled to free himself. As time went on, Kai found himself withdrawing from activities and places that reminded him of the accident. He stopped going to the pub with his mates, unable to stomach the smell of beer or the sound of laughter and music. His relationships began to suffer, particularly with his wife, who couldn't understand why he was becoming increasingly distant and withdrawn. At work, Kai's avoidance behaviors started to take a toll on his performance as a welder. He'd get anxious around loud machinery or when working on projects that involved cars, which made it difficult for him to focus and complete tasks efficiently. His boss noticed the decline in his productivity and started to question whether Kai was still up to the job. It wasn't until Kai had a heart-to-heart with his wife, Leilani, that he realized just how much his symptoms were controlling his life. She expressed her concerns about their relationship and encouraged Kai to seek help. With her support, Kai finally made the decision to see a therapist, hoping to break free from the grip of his PTSD and learn to live with the memories of that fateful night without being consumed by them. As Kai sat in the therapist's office, he couldn't help but feel a sense of trepidation about what lay ahead. Would he be able to confront his demons and overcome the trauma that had been holding him back for so long? Only time would tell, but for now, he was willing to take that first step towards healing, no matter how daunting it seemed.
